messages.author: cf7ff2ca88472595
messages.subject: Unmatched degrees of freedom
parts:
Hi all
I have a question about using lavaan to replicate a growth curve model I have done in an Amos SEM class. The degrees of freedom of the two models (between R and Amos) are not the same. So I think I may do something wrong but cannot tell it from my syntax.
I really appreciate any kind of help.
Thanks!
Xiguang Liu

messages.author: 99a06696c483481a
messages.subject: Re: Unmatched degrees of freedom
parts:
Look at the full summary(model1) to see which parameters are being estimated. My first guess is that, perhaps, lavaan did not constrain residual variances to equality, while Amos did. That would account for the 4 DF difference.

With p = 5 observed variables, I am figuring DF as:
unique variances and covariances: p * (p + 1) / 2 = 15
observed variable means:               p                     =   5
Total 20 possible DF.

Your Amos output suggests that the parameters being estimated are
mean and variance for both ICEPT and SLOPE -- that's 4
covariance of ICEPT with SLOPE:                                 +1
common residual variance for all observed variables    +1

That would give DF = 20 - 6 = 14.

If lavaan did not constrain observed variable residual variances to equality, that would mean estimating 5 residual variances instead of 1, so DF would be lower by 4, giving DF = 10.

messages.author: 99a06696c483481a
messages.subject: Re: Unmatched degrees of freedom
parts:
You could specify equality in residual variances via:

ocesdt2~~a*ocesdt2
ocesdt3~~a*ocesdt3
ocesdt4~~a*ocesdt4
ocesdt5~~a*ocesdt5
ocesdt6~~a*ocesdt6

Using the same label a for all of these parameter estimates constrains them to equality, so that you are estimating 1 parameter rather than 5. I am sure that there are more efficient coding approaches.

messages.author: 99a06696c483481a
messages.subject: Re: Unmatched degrees of freedom
parts:
I have not used Amos in a very long time. But my thoughts:

How much different?

If "a little different"--
Different packages are "tuned" to perform best under different conditions. I am not familiar with how Amos is tuned. Differences with lavaan could produce small differences in results, especially if n is small and model fit is not so good. Your Amos chi-square was 205 with 14 DF--that's not very good. lavaan has options to mimic Mplus, EQS and LISREL, I believe, but not an option to mimic Amos.

If "a lot different"
My first guess would be differences in standardization or management of variances for either common factors or for specific factors / error terms. Lay the results out side by side. Start by examining the covariance matrices of the common factors and the error terms.

Beyond this, I'm not sure.
--Ed Rigdon
